scope:
Measure FP32 matrix-reduction error with exactly BF16-representable inputs.

Seed62 matches the earlier matrix probe. All native storage remains FP32;
only the reduction length changes, using prefixes of the same original data.
This is a synthetic mechanism diagnostic, not learned-model attribution.
finding: Exact BF16-representable FP32-stored input sweep records native matrix reduction error acrossK1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128, with exact input roundtrips/repeats and no fallback. K1/32/128 are bitwise previous fresh HiFi4 outputs. K1=0, K2=0.00013973952, K4=0.00022777611, K8=0.0003097191, K16=0.00031117151, K32=0.00031307106, K64=0.00040936116, K128=0.00074520998. This isolates additional loss beyond initial operand representability without identifying every internal rounding point.
timing_limit: Warm synchronized output-transfer-inclusive samples retained as diagnostic metadata, not an optimization speed claim. Different K can select different native lowering/kernel strategies.
decision: Use measured short-K accuracy to select the next decomposition experiment. Do not assume BF16-representable FP32 inputs or fp32_dest_acc_en guarantee an accurate long reduction. Keep kernel reload hypothesis distinct from demonstrated behavior.
